A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete scientific appendices are readable and directly matchable; v2 additionally contains a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations on THINGS odd-one-out, model-recovery simulations, and regression analyses in Section 3 and the supplementary figures and tables.

after.justification: V2 retains the original behavioral-data analyses, model-recovery simulations, and regression results, including the supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: The linear-probing objective, scalar-matrix shrinkage regularizer, temperature calibration, and model-recovery procedure are unchanged. Section 2.1 rewords the regularization paragraph and adds a citation without changing Equation 4 or the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same THINGS odd-one-out data and synthetic odd-one-out scenarios. The ImageNet-1K validation data used for PCA in Figure S3 are also retained; no dataset or task coverage is added.

E2.justification: The same 20 primary candidate models and 10 additional models appear in Tables S1 and S5 and their corresponding comparisons. The regularization and evaluation-flexibility comparisons are unchanged; the newly cited works are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the same image-disjoint three-fold evaluation, triplet sampling, training-set sizes, transformation configurations, calibration target, and metrics. The new checklist points to existing settings without revising them.

E4.justification: The regularizer comparison, 500-component PCA control, expanded-model and grouped-recovery analyses, representational-geometry analyses, and alternative dimensionality regression already appear in v1. Figures S1–S6 and Tables S2–S4 retain these analyses unchanged.

E5.justification: The 30-seed main simulations, 10,000 model-level bootstrap replicates, confidence intervals, and multiple-comparison corrections are unchanged. Checklist item 7 summarizes existing error bars and significance reporting rather than introducing a new statistical practice.

E6.justification: The numerical entries and plotted results in Figures 1–5, S1–S6, and Tables S1–S5 are unchanged. For example, Table S1 retains full-transform accuracies of 0.5959 for OpenAI CLIP RN50 and 0.5927 for ViT L/16, and Figure 1 retains recovery below 80%.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and appendices are retained, including Lemma 1 and its scalar-matrix shrinkage proof, noise-ceiling calibration, model-recovery definitions, and dimensionality formulas. The checklist references the existing proof without adding theoretical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introductory contributions, and discussion retain the same claims about imperfect recovery, representational shifts, effective dimensionality, and the predictive-accuracy–identifiability trade-off. No central claim is strengthened or narrowed.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including restriction to behavioral odd-one-out data, uncertain generalization to neural measurements, dependence on the candidate set, and the limitations of closed-set recovery. The checklist adds no substantive scientific qualification.

D1.justification: Checklist items 5 and 12 add statements about a submitted code/data ZIP with reproduction instructions and THINGS usage restrictions. The existing GitHub availability statement and Appendices A.7–A.8 remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish a new public release.

R1.justification: V2 adds Braun, Grant, and Saxe on functional versus representational similarity and Muttenthaler et al., Aligning machine and human visual representations across abstraction levels, cited beside the regularizer. Other reference edits mainly update publication metadata for already-cited works.

P1.justification: V2 makes a localized rewrite of the regularization paragraph, updates bibliography entries, and appends a NeurIPS checklist. The scientific narrative and section organization remain intact, with no extensive rewriting or restructuring.

P2.justification: The bibliography reflows, and the appended checklist introduces numbered questions, answers, and guideline lists. Existing figures and tables retain their graphics, structure, and placement, apart from citation-number updates.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves research attribution through two relevant citations and adds explicit asset-use disclosures absent from v1. These are limited documentation gains; the scientific evidence and conclusions are unchanged. The checklist's promise of a future GitHub release sits awkwardly beside the retained statement that code and data are already available, limiting the improvement in access clarity.
